title: Design System: MD Manager Projects viewer (Calm)

tokenCarrier.element: <main class="workspace workspace-projects projects-shell" data-testid="projects-workspace"> in src/projects/ProjectsView.tsx
tokenCarrier.note: Calm tokens are not on :root, so snippets use var(--token, light-hex) fallbacks to render outside the shell. focus, attention, edge and danger-text are app-level :root tokens (index.css, run.css).

headline.purpose: Page titles (h2): the run header title, the Runs home heading.

title.purpose: h3/h4 inside nodes, activity phase names, card summary lines.

body.purpose: Running text and finding messages; inherits line-height 1.45 from index.css :root.

body-dense.purpose: Facts, captions, card context, finding fields; siblings at 0.9rem and 0.875rem fill the same role.

label.purpose: Uppercase section headers in --muted; smaller variants for rail titles, day rows and figure labels.

figure.purpose: Values in a node figures row, tabular numbers.

mono.purpose: Commands and raw messages (--font-mono); run ids use it at 0.95rem 600-700, severity chips at 11px 600.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Hairline lift on cards, figures, the run header and the node area in light.

shadows.name: shadow-dark
shadows.purpose: The dark scheme sets --shadow to none; depth comes from surface steps.

motion.name: ui-pulse
motion.purpose: The dot of a live running chip; only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

breakpoints.name: rail-row
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the rail moves above the content as a row of pills.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: graph hidden, rows stack, 44px targets, 10px workspace padding.

breakpoints.name: steps-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: container query on the Steps section: rows wrap to two lines.

breakpoints.name: board-split
breakpoints.purpose: Pipeline and Steps side by side when the compact graph at its 0.83 floor and a 400px Steps column fit (node/board.ts).

narrative.overview:
_The qualitative language in this file (the North Star, the descriptive names, the philosophy lines) was inferred by the documenting session on 2026-10-08 from the code and `docs/PRD_VIEWER_REVAMP.md`, and can be revised by the operator._

The Projects viewer is a desk one operator sits at between other work: a cool, neutral surface where every sheet is laid out the same way and nothing competes for the eye except what changed. The look is the "Calm" set of tokens chosen on 2026-10-02 (the "Bold" alternative was removed); it is flat, dense and quiet, so that the few coloured marks on a page are the answer to "what needs me, what failed, what is moving".

Structure comes from sections, weight and hairline borders, never from decoration. Every page is a stack of sections with one small-caps header each, cards and rows with a 4 px stripe in their state's tone, and monospace for identifiers and commands. Colour is a vocabulary of six state tones and three severities, applied identically on chips, stripes, rail dots, graph nodes, step bars and finding cards; the single cool-blue accent is kept for links, focus and pressed controls and never says anything about a run.

Both colour schemes are first-class. The light values in the frontmatter are canonical; the dark scheme redefines every Calm token on the same element with lighter, desaturated tones over a near-black blue surface, and drops the only shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Cool neutral surfaces (page, card, inset) separated by 1 px hairlines; effectively flat.
One accent hue, never used for state.
Six state tones plus three severities, each as a strong colour and a soft background pair.
A 4 px tone stripe on the left of cards, rows and activity groups, and on the top of run and node headers.
A text glyph or a word repeats every state that colour shows.
System font stacks only; small uppercase labels for section headers; tabular numbers for times and counts.
Dense desktop rhythm (2 to 20 px), 44 px tap targets and a single column on phones.

rules.name: The State-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour on a Projects page means state and only state: the six tones and three severities. Structure, grouping and emphasis come from sections, weight and borders, never from a tint.

rules.name: The Accent-Is-Not-A-State Rule
rules.body: The accent hue is never a tone. A link, a focus ring or a pressed button is blue; a running run is Signal Blue from its own token, and no status ever borrows `accent`.

rules.name: The One Mapping Rule
rules.body: Every element drawn in a tone takes it from the one mapping in `src/projects/tone.ts` (`statusTone`, `attentionTone`, `severityTone`, `stateTone`); an unknown status is idle, an unknown severity is P2, and an attention wins over a status, so a running run that waits on the operator is Needs-You Amber everywhere.

rules.name: The Soft-Pair Rule
rules.body: Tone text sits only on its own soft background, at 4.5:1 or better in both schemes. A link on a tinted card takes Desk Ink, underlined, because the accent can fall under 4.5:1 there.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: System font stacks only; no web font request. A new face is a separate decision, not a refinement.

rules.name: The Small-Caps Header Rule
rules.body: A section is named by one uppercase 13 px Pencil Grey label at 600 with 0.08em tracking, with an optional one-line sub-header of counts and tools pushed right. Section headers are never coloured and never banded.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Times, durations, counts and figures set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so columns of them align.

rules.name: The No Page Scroll Rule
rules.body: Nothing widens the page: anything wider than the column scrolls inside its own container.

rules.name: The Flat Desk Rule
rules.body: Surfaces do not lift on hover or focus; hover changes the fill to Inset Grey, focus draws an outline. No new shadow is added for state.

rules.name: The Stripe Rule
rules.body: A container shows its state as one 4 px edge in its tone (left on cards and rows, top on headers) over a neutral Sheet White body; only the Now banner, blocking cards and chips fill with the soft tone.

rules.name: The Dash-For-Executor Rule
rules.body: On the workflow graph the outline's dash says who executes a step (solid for an agent, `8 4` for the trusted verifier, `3 3` for the controller) and colour says its status; neither ever carries the other's meaning.

rules.name: The Glyph Repeats Rule
rules.body: Wherever a tone appears, a glyph or a word says the same state: ✓ succeeded, ✗ failed, ● running, ○ pending or cancelled, ‖ paused, ? waiting on the operator, plus the chip text or a dot's title. Colour never carries state alone.

rules.name: The Attention Ring Rule
rules.body: A step or run that waits on the operator keeps its own status colour and adds Attention Amber on top (a ring, a `?` glyph, an inset rule); the wait is shown, the status is not rewritten.

rules.name: The Selection Is Not State Rule
rules.body: Selection and the current item are drawn in Desk Ink (a thick outline, an inner ring, 600 weight), never in a tone and never in Signal Blue.

dos: **Do** take every colour inside the Projects viewer from the Calm tokens on `.projects-shell`, and define new tokens there with a dark counterpart under both dark selectors.
**Do** route every state through `tone.ts` and draw it with the tone classes (`tone-ok`, `tone-run`, `tone-warn`, `tone-fail`, `tone-pause`, `tone-idle`, `sev-p0` to `sev-p2`).
**Do** pair every tone with a glyph or a word, and keep tone text on its own soft background at 4.5:1 or better in both schemes.
**Do** show a container's state as a 4 px stripe in its tone over Sheet White, and use the soft fill only for chips, the Now banner and blocking cards.
**Do** name each section with one uppercase 13 px Pencil Grey label, a one-line sub-header and tools on the right.
**Do** set identifiers and commands in the monospace stack, and give every command its own Copy button outside the command text.
**Do** keep 44 px tap targets and a single scroll-free column at phone width; let wide content scroll inside its own box.
donts: **Don't** use the accent (Desk Blue) for any status, and don't use Signal Blue for anything but running.
